arxiv-2103-04479.title: Secrecy Performance of Small-Cell Networks with Transmitter Selection and Unreliable Backhaul under Spectrum Sharing Environment Part of this work was presented in the 13th EAI International Conference on Cognitive Radio Oriented Wireless Networks (CROWNCOM), Ghent, Belgium, Sep. 2018. Jinghua Zhang
arxiv-2103-04479.creator: Jinghua Zhang, Chinmoy Kundu, Octavia A. Dobre, Emi Garcia-Palacios, Nguyen-Son Vo, Jinghua Zhang, Chinmoy Kundu, Octavia A. Dobre, Emiliano Garcia-Palacios, and Nguyen-Son Vo
arxiv-2103-04479.description: Abstract We investigate the secrecy performance of an underlay small-cell cognitive radio network under unreliable backhaul connections. The small-cell network shares the same spectrum with the primary network, ensuring that a desired outage probability constraint is always met in the primary network.

arxiv-2109-08994.title: ReaSCAN: Compositional Reasoning in Language Grounding
arxiv-2109-08994.creator: Zhengxuan WuStanford University wuzhengx@stanford.edu, Elisa KreissStanford University ekreiss@stanford.edu Desmond C. OngNational University of Singapore& IHPC, A*STAR dco@comp.nus.edu.sg Christopher PottsStanford University cgpotts@stanford.edu
arxiv-2109-08994.description: Abstract The ability to compositionally map language to referents, relations, and actions is an essential component of language understanding. The recent gSCAN dataset (Ruis et al. 2020, NeurIPS ) is an inspiring attempt to assess the capacity of models to learn this kind of grounding in scenarios involving navigational instructions.

arxiv-2110-08228.title: Cross-Domain Data Integration for Named Entity Disambiguation in Biomedical Text
arxiv-2110-08228.creator: Maya Varma, Laurel Orr, Sen Wu, Megan Leszczynski, Xiao Ling, Christopher Ré
arxiv-2110-08228.description: Abstract Named entity disambiguation (NED), which involves mapping textual mentions to structured entities, is particularly challenging in the medical domain due to the presence of rare entities. Existing approaches are limited by the presence of coarse-grained structural resources in biomedical knowledge bases as well as the use of training datasets that provide low coverage over uncommon resources.

arxiv-2202-02862.title: Asymptotic behavior of the forecast–assimilation process with unstable dynamics
arxiv-2202-02862.creator: Dan Crisan, Michael Ghil
arxiv-2202-02862.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dan Crisan, Michael Ghil. Extensive numerical evidence shows that the assimilation of observations has a stabilizing effect on unstable dynamics, in numerical weather prediction and elsewhere. In this paper, we apply mathematically rigorous methods to showing why this is so. Our stabilization results do not assume a full set of observations and we provide examples where it suffices to observe the model’s unstable degrees of freedom. This paper is dedicated to the memory of Anna Trevisan and to her contributions to data assimilation



V.

arxiv-2204-07236.title: A* shortest string decoding for non-idempotent semirings
arxiv-2204-07236.creator: Kyle Gorman & Cyril Allauzen
arxiv-2204-07236.description: Abstract The single shortest path algorithm is undefined for weighted finite-state automata over non-idempotent semirings because such semirings do not guarantee the existence of a shortest path. However, in non-idempotent semirings admitting an order satisfying a monotonicity condition (such as the plus-times or log semirings), the shortest string is well-defined.

arxiv-2211-02039.title: The Projected Covariance Measure for assumption-lean variable significance testing
arxiv-2211-02039.creator: Anton Rask Lundborg †⋄ , Ilmun Kim †⋆ , Rajen D. Shah † and Richard J. Samworth †
arxiv-2211-02039.description: Abstract Testing the significance of a variable or group of variables X X for predicting a response Y Y , given additional covariates Z Z , is a ubiquitous task in statistics. A simple but common approach is to specify a linear model, and then test whether the regression coefficient for X X is non-zero.

arxiv-2212-07343.title: Universal characters twisted by roots of unity
arxiv-2212-07343.creator: Seamus P. Albion
arxiv-2212-07343.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Seamus P. Albion. A classical result of Littlewood gives a factorisation for the Schur function at a set of variables “twisted” by a primitive t t -th root of unity, characterised by the core and quotient of the indexing partition. While somewhat neglected, it has proved to be an important tool in the character theory of the symmetric group, the cyclic sieving phenomenon, plethysms of symmetric functions and more.

arxiv-2306-03907.title: CL-UZH at SemEval-2023 Task 10: Sexism Detection through Incremental Fine-Tuning and Multi-Task Learning with Label Descriptions
arxiv-2306-03907.creator: Janis Goldzycher
arxiv-2306-03907.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Janis Goldzycher. The widespread popularity of social media has led to an increase in hateful, abusive, and sexist language, motivating methods for the automatic detection of such phenomena. The goal of the SemEval shared task Towards Explainable Detection of Online Sexism (EDOS 2023) is to detect sexism in English social media posts (subtask A), and to categorize such posts into four coarse-grained sexism categories (subtask B), and eleven fine-grained subcategories (subtask C).

arxiv-2309-11716.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrew Jacobs, Stylianos Nikas, John Ash, Behnam Ashrafkhani, Ivana Belosovic, Julian Bergmann, Callum Brown, Jaime Cardona, Eleanor Dunling, Timo Dickel, Luca Egoriti, Gabriella Gelinas, Zach Hockenbery, Sakshi Kakkar, Brian Kootte, Ali Mollaebrahimi, Eleni Marina Lykiardopoulou, Tobias Murböck, St. The prediction of isotopic abundances resulting from the rapid neutron capture process (r-process) requires high-precision mass measurements. arxiv-2402-12379.title: A SPIRED code for the reconstruction of spin distribution Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2402-12379.creator: Simon Buchwald, Gabriele Ciaramella, Julien Salomon, Dominique Sugny
arxiv-2402-12379.description: Abstract In Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR), it is of crucial importance to have an accurate knowledge of the sample probability distribution corresponding to inhomogeneities of the magnetic fields. An accurate identification of the sample distribution requires a set of experimental data that is sufficiently rich to extract all fundamental information.

arxiv-2403-12639.title: Imaging and spectroscopic observations of a confined solar filament eruption with two-stage evolution 2023 Imaging and spectroscopic observations of a confined solar filament eruption with two-stage evolution – References
arxiv-2403-12639.creator: Zhe Xu Xiaoli Yan, Liheng Yang, Zhike Xue Jincheng Wang Yian Zhou
arxiv-2403-12639.description: Abstract Solar filament eruptions are often characterized by stepwise evolution due to the involvement of multiple mechanisms, such as magnetohydrodynamic instabilities and magnetic reconnection. In this article, we investigated a confined filament eruption with a distinct two-stage evolution by using the imaging and spectroscopic observations from the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO).

arxiv-2410-01925.title: Topological mapping for traversability-aware long-range navigation in off-road terrain
arxiv-2410-01925.creator: Jean-François Tremblay, Julie Alhosh, Louis Petit, Faraz Lotfi, Lara Landauro, David Meger
arxiv-2410-01925.description: Abstract Autonomous robots navigating in off-road terrain like forests open new opportunities for automation. While off-road navigation has been studied, existing work often relies on clearly delineated pathways. We present a method allowing for long-range planning, exploration and low-level control in unknown off-trail forest terrain, using vision and GPS only.

arxiv-2504-00883.title: Improved Visual-Spatial Reasoning via R1-Zero-Like Training
arxiv-2504-00883.creator: Zhenyi Liao, Qingsong Xie, Yanhao Zhang, Zijian Kong, Haonan Lu, Zhenyu Yang, Zhijie Deng
arxiv-2504-00883.description: Abstract Increasing attention has been placed on improving the reasoning capacities of multi-modal large language models (MLLMs). As the cornerstone for AI agents that function in the physical realm, video-based visual-spatial intelligence (VSI) emerges as one of the most pivotal reasoning capabilities of MLLMs.

arxiv-2506-10905.title: Physical properties of R R Co 2 Al 8 ( R = R= La, Ce, Pr, Nd and Sm) single crystals: an emerging structure-type for anisotropic Kondo lattice studies
arxiv-2506-10905.creator: Fernando A. Garcia 1,2,3 , Sushma Kumari 1,2 , Juan Schmidt 1,2 , Cris Adriano 2 , Aashish Sapkota 1 , Paul C. Canfield 1,2 , Rebecca Flint 1,2 and Raquel A. Ribeiro 1,2
arxiv-2506-10905.description: Abstract Systematic investigations of rare-earth ( R R ) based intermetallic materials is a leading strategy to reveal the underlying mechanisms governing a range of physical phenomena, such as the formation of a Kondo lattice and competing electronic and magnetic anisotropies.

arxiv-2601-20753.title: GraphAllocBench: A Flexible Benchmark for Preference-Conditioned Multi-Objective Policy Learning
arxiv-2601-20753.creator: Zhiheng Jiang, Yunzhe Wang, Ryan Marr, Ellen Novoseller, Benjamin T. Files, Volkan Ustun
arxiv-2601-20753.description: Abstract Preference-Conditioned Policy Learning (PCPL) in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) aims to approximate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions by conditioning policies on user-specified preferences over objectives. This enables a single model to flexibly adapt to arbitrary trade-offs at run-time by producing a policy on or near the Pareto front.

pmc-10693000.title: Pollinator sharing and hybridization in a pair of dioecious figs sheds light on the pathways to speciation
pmc-10693000.creator: Jian-Feng Huang, Jenjira Fungjanthuek, Ming-Bo Chen, Gui-Xiang Liu, Yi-Yi Dong, Yan-Qiong Peng, Bo Wang, Simon T Segar
pmc-10693000.description: The dynamics and processes underlying the codiversification of plant–pollinator interactions are of great interest to researchers of biodiversity and evolution. Cospeciation is generally considered a key process driving the diversity of figs and their pollinating wasps. Groups of closely related figs pollinated by separate wasps occur frequently and represent excellent opportunities to study ongoing diversification in this textbook mutualism.

pmc-11363540.title: Impact of early diagnosis on surgical outcomes in patients with Loeys-Dietz syndrome
pmc-11363540.creator: Hongsun Kim, Jun Ho Lee, Su Ryeun Chung, Pyo Won Park, Taek Kyu Park, I-Seok Kang, June Huh, Duk-Kyung Kim, Yang Hyun Cho, Kiick Sung
pmc-11363540.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to investigate the influence of early diagnosis (ED) on surgical outcomes in patients definitively diagnosed with Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS).MethodsA retrospective review was conducted on 38 patients with LDS who underwent aortic surgery at our institution between January 1995 and June 2022. The primary endpoint was freedom from aortic reoperation.

pmc-11583081.creator: Leland L Fleming, Matthew K Defenderfer, Pinar Demirayak, Paul Stewart, Dawn K Decarlo, Kristina M Visscher
pmc-11583081.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Human behavior can be remarkably shaped by experience, such as the removal of sensory input. Many studies of conditions such as stroke, limb amputation, and vision loss have examined how removal of input changes brain function. However, an important question yet to be answered is: when input is lost, does the brain change its connectivity to preferentially use some remaining inputs over others?

pmc-12565918.title: The Influence of Reactive Ion Etching Chemistry on the Initial Resistance and Cycling Stability of Line-Type (Bridge) Phase-Change Memory Devices
pmc-12565918.creator: Abbas Espiari, Henriette Padberg, Alexander Kiehn, Kristoffer Schnieders, Jiayuan Zhang, Gregor Mussler, Stefan Wiefels, Abdur Rehman Jalil, Detlev Grützmacher, Linfeng Lan
pmc-12565918.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Phase-change memory (PCM) is a promising candidate for in-memory computation and neuromorphic computing due to its high endurance, low cycle-to-cycle variability, and low read noise. However, among other factors, its performance strongly depends on the post-lithography fabrication steps. This study examines the impact of reactive ion etching (RIE) on PCM device performance by evaluating different etching gas mixtures, CHF3:O2, H2:Ar, and Ar, and determining their impact on key device characteristics, particularly initial resistance and cycling stability.

pmc-12590727.title: Synchronous bone and adrenal extramedullary plasmacytoma: a rare case report and literature review

pmc-12590727.description: BackgroundAdrenal extramedullary plasmacytoma (EMP) is an exceptionally rare plasma cell neoplasm with fewer than 20 documented cases worldwide. The clinical presentation, optimal management strategies, and long-term outcomes remain poorly defined.Case presentationWe report the case of a 51-year-old woman with synchronous bone and adrenal EMP, without multiple myeloma.

pmc-13615539.title: MCOD: a memory-constrained deep learning framework for robust outlier detection in quantitative proteomics
pmc-13615539.creator: Jinze Huang, Huanyue Liao, Bo Meng, Guangkui Fan, Dong An, Xinhua Dai, Xiang Fang, Yang Zhao
pmc-13615539.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ensuring robust quality control (QC) remains a major challenge in quantitative proteomics, particularly in detecting and managing outliers. Deep learning offers powerful representational capacity for ultra-high-dimensional data but often suffers from overfitting in small-sample scenarios. To address this, we propose memory-constrained outlier detection (MCOD), a deep anomaly detection framework that directly processes MaxQuant outputs and achieves competitive recall at high precision levels, which suggests a reduced risk of overlooking true outliers.

pmc-13676271.title: Successful management of high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy during pregnancy with intravitreal faricimab
pmc-13676271.creator: Sonia Scallon, Michael Rauser, Anny M S Cheng, Kakarla V Chalam
pmc-13676271.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Management of proliferative diabetic retinopathy during pregnancy requires balancing maternal vision preservation against uncertain fetal risks associated with intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy. We report a 27-year-old woman with a chronic type 1 diabetes mellitus who presented at 28 weeks and 1 day of gestation with high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy and dense vitreous hemorrhage in the left eye, precluding panretinal photocoagulation.
